hook: Cars that run on *100% ethanol* are now legal to certify in India
tldr: The road transport ministry amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to recognise E100 (nearly pure ethanol) alongside E85, giving carmakers a path to certify flex-fuel vehicles. E20 has been the default petrol since April 2025.

beats.what: Rules 115 and 115E now include E100. Flex-fuel vehicles can run on petrol, any ethanol blend, or pure ethanol.
beats.why: India is cutting oil imports with ethanol. Blends above E20 (E22–E30) were specified in May 2026.
beats.care: Nothing changes at your pump yet. Check your vehicle's fuel sticker and manual before using any higher blend.

cards.body: "This is an enabling step, not a market outcome," says Amit Bhatt of the International Council on Clean Transportation. Carmakers still have to build and certify these vehicles.

cards.q: What's the default petrol blend in India since April 2025?
